name: De Vinne 8pt 1897
designer: Unidentified in the retained source pages
foundry: Shown by the United States Government Printing Office; 1897 stock mark Keystone–10
description: Eight-point De Vinne with flared serifs, a sweeping Q tail, double-storey a and g, and observed mixed-height figures. Seven named alternates retain source variations.
character_set_notes: Complete observed A–Z, a–z and ten figures, with period, comma and the double-bar historical hyphen encoded as hyphen-minus. Space has a modern layout advance. Seven observed alternatives are unencoded glyphs available through stylistic sets; no unsupported character is inferred. 7 whole observed diagonal fractions, cent and percent are also encoded. Fraction row-center placement is a modern layout convention, independent of historical baseline evidence. Source-quality gaps: U+2154, U+215D; these companions remain unencoded. The matching poster specimens supply the observed colon, semicolon and right single quotation mark used as an apostrophe; no ASCII apostrophe or opening quotation mark is inferred.
observed: The 1897 specimen supplies both complete eight-point alphabets. Matching census, job-room and document impressions supply clearer letters, all ten figures and punctuation. The census M, four 1897 figures and lining document three are retained as named alternatives. The census figure designs define the default sequence, with cleaner matching 1897 zero, six, eight and nine; unequal source positions are preserved. Matching ATF assortments supply whole 8-point diagonal fractions and symbols; exact selected pages, crops, thresholds and scale measurements are retained. A broad, flatter S appears beside a narrow S in the BYU eight-point poster. The complete BYU broad impression is retained as an unencoded alternate. The BYU eight-point poster supplies a clearer whole U with intact flared heads and right stem, replacing the weaker Census impression. Matching ATF poster specimens supply the whole colon, semicolon and right single quotation mark used as an apostrophe at measured capital scale and native text-row baselines.
reconstructed: No visible form is invented. Uniform source-page scaling, measured rigid baseline rotation, local paper correction and modern spacing prepare the observed forms. No cross-size substitution or independent width stretching. Fraction row-center placement at 350 is a modern layout choice; no historical text baseline is established by the charts. No fraction parts are assembled or redrawn.

revival.author: Harold Lehmann
revival.notes: All visible forms are observed. Four-times Lanczos source sampling preserves small serifs during curve fitting; 71 exact derived crops retain native JP2 coordinates and hashes. Uniform page scales and measured row/numeral baseline rotations preserve optical proportions. Seven named alternatives use ss01/ss02/ss03/ss04; ss04 selects the broad S. No holes are filled and no visible form is drawn. See source/METHOD.md. The whole fraction companions retain their full physical source dimensions and deliberate slash interruptions. Existing outlines, spacing and named alternatives are preserved. U retains the same construction from the clearer BYU poster, at independently measured scale and native baseline. Its advance increases from 707 to 744 to preserve observed width with the same 35-unit sidebearings; all other outlines and advances remain unchanged. Whole punctuation companions retain observed row-relative positions, independently measured scale and modern 35-unit sidebearings. Exact evidence and quality limits are recorded in source/punctuation-review.json.
